what: Teradyne makes the machines that test chips after they are manufactured, checking each one works before it is shipped. It also owns Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots, which make collaborative factory robots.
customers: Chipmakers and their assembly partners, electronics manufacturers, and factories buying robots.
money: testers for logic, memory and analogue chips
collaborative robot arms and autonomous mobile robots
moat: Test platforms that chipmakers qualify into their production flows, where the cost of switching testers mid-product-life is prohibitive.
risks: Chip test demand is cyclical and swung hard in recent years
Revenue has been flat over three years
The robotics business has grown more slowly than expected
Smartphone test demand depends on a small number of customers
opportunities: Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
AI chips are large and complex, which raises test time and therefore tester demand
Return on invested capital of 19% with almost no debt
watch: Semiconductor test orders, especially for AI and high-performance computing chips.
